newsitem.title: USA: U.S. travelers group rates safety of 260 airlines.
newsitem.headline: U.S. travelers group rates safety of 260 airlines.

text.p: A new organization representing air travelers has begun compiling safety ratings for airlines around the world and has failed 29 of them, its founder said on Tuesday.
The Air Travelers Association issued its first Airline Safety Report Card based on the fatal accident history of 260 carriers in 107 countries.

The worst crash to flight ratios were attributed to Aviateca (Guatemala), COPA Panama, Aero Peru, Lan Chile, Lauda Air (Austria), Aeroflot Russian International, ADC Airlines (Nigeria), Air Mauritanie (Mauritania), Ethiopian Airlines, China Northwest Airlines and Xiamen Airlines (China).

The only U.S. airline to be given a failing grade was ValuJet Airlines, the low-fare carrier that was grounded last year after one of its DC-9s crashed in the Florida Everglades, killing all 110 people aboard.

"It is easier for travelers to obtain advance information about in-flight meals or movies, than it is to find out about the safety record of the airlines they are going to fly," said aviation attorney and association founder David Stempler.
The safety report covers airlines that use Western-built jet aircraft and operated at least 20,000 flights between January 1987 and December 1996.
The number of fatal accidents was divided by the number of flights and a formula applied to produce a grade.
Although US Airways had six fatal crashes during the period, its large number of flights still enabled it to achieve an A grade, like the bulk of U.S. airlines.
The idea of grading airlines for safety has periodically been discussed but the airline industry and the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration have said it would be hard to implement objectively.
But Stempler insists his report is objective, being based purely on numbers. "It's not perfect but it's the only thing out there," he said.
"Although past performance is not a predictor of future performance, it is a good bet that airlines that have done well over the last ten years will continue to do so."
The Air Travelers Association will compile the airline report card at least twice a year and hopes to fund itself through consumer members.
In addition to serving as an advocacy organization for airline passengers, the association will encourage the public and aviation employees to report airline safety issues.
The association can be contacted on the Internet at www.1800airsafe.com or at 1-800-247-7233.
